summary.title: Performance Hints and Thread Scheduling
summary.one_liner: OpenVINO's CPU plugin picks thread, core-type and pinning defaults from a LATENCY or THROUGHPUT performance hint, and this page explains those defaults and how to override them.
keywords: how to set thread count for openvino
takeaways: Use the LATENCY or THROUGHPUT performance hint for portable CPU tuning instead of setting low-level properties by hand.
With the latency hint, the default core type depends on model precision (INT8 vs FP32) and the ratio of E-cores to P-cores; hyper-threading is set to No and a single socket is used by default.
With the throughput hint, threads per stream depend on the model's memory pressure (low, medium, high), and num_streams is derived from inference_num_threads divided by that value.
Properties such as inference_num_threads, scheduling_core_type, enable_hyper_threading and enable_cpu_pinning can limit CPU resources, with Python and C++ examples given.
When mixing oneTBB and OpenMP in one pipeline, busy-waiting can waste cores; options include using oneTBB everywhere, rebuilding with OpenMP, or setting OMP_WAIT_POLICY to PASSIVE.
summary.summary: The page documents how OpenVINO's CPU plugin uses the LATENCY and THROUGHPUT performance hints to set low-level threading properties such as inference_num_threads, num_streams, scheduling_core_type, hyper-threading and CPU pinning. It gives tables of default P-core and E-core choices by model precision and core ratio for the latency hint, and threads-per-stream choices by memory pressure for the throughput hint, with separate Windows and Linux defaults. It also includes Python and C++ snippets for limiting CPU resources, notes that scheduling_core_type and enable_hyper_threading only apply to x86-64 on Linux and Windows, and discusses oneTBB versus OpenMP busy-wait overhead.
